passages.text: Put the ram’s horn to your lips! An eagle looms over the house of the LORD, because the people have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His prophet.
God commands, "Put the ram’s horn to your lips."
An eagle stands over the house of the LORD.
This happens because the people broke My covenant.
The people rebelled against My law.
passages.original: אֶל־ חִכְּךָ֣ שֹׁפָ֔ר כַּנֶּ֖שֶׁר עַל־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה יַ֚עַן עָבְר֣וּ בְרִיתִ֔י וְעַל־ תּוֹרָתִ֖י פָּשָֽׁעוּ׃

passages.text: Israel cries out to Me, “O our God, we know You!”
passages.sermon:
Israel speaks to God.
Israel cries out to God.
Israel says, "O our God, we know You."
Israel claims to know God.

passages.text: But Israel has rejected good; an enemy will pursue him.
passages.sermon: Israel has rejected what is good.\r\nAn enemy will chase Israel.

passages.text: They set up kings, but not by Me. They make princes, but without My approval. With their silver and gold they make themselves idols, to their own destruction.
passages.sermon:
Israel is the subject.
Israel set up kings.
I did not appoint these kings.
Israel made princes.
I did not approve these princes.
Israel used their silver and gold.
They made idols for themselves.
These idols will lead to their destruction.
passages.original: הֵ֤ם הִמְלִיכוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מִמֶּ֔נִּי הֵשִׂ֖ירוּ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עְתִּי כַּסְפָּ֣ם וּזְהָבָ֗ם עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים לְמַ֖עַן יִכָּרֵֽת׃

passages.text: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
passages.sermon:
God rejected the calf idol of Samaria.
God’s anger burns against the people of Samaria.
The people cannot become innocent.
God asks, “How long will they be unable to be innocent?”
passages.original: זָנַח֙ עֶגְלֵ֣ךְ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן חָרָ֥ה אַפִּ֖י בָּ֑ם עַד־ מָתַ֕י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ נִקָּיֹֽן׃

passages.text: For this thing is from Israel— a craftsman made it, and it is not God. It will be broken to pieces, that calf of Samaria.
passages.sermon:
Israel made this thing.
A craftsman made it.
This thing is not God.
The calf of Samaria will be broken to pieces.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְה֔וּא חָרָ֣שׁ עָשָׂ֔הוּ וְלֹ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים ה֑וּא כִּֽי־ שְׁבָבִ֣ים יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עֵ֖גֶל שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind. There is no standing grain; what sprouts fails to yield flour. Even if it should produce, the foreigners would swallow it up.
passages.sermon:
Israel acts foolishly.
They plant nothing of value.
They sow the wind.
They will harvest disaster.
They will reap the whirlwind.
They have no standing grain.
Nothing grows for them.
What sprouts does not make flour.
If anything does grow,
Foreigners will take it away.
Foreigners will swallow it up.
passages.original: כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ יִזְרָ֖עוּ וְסוּפָ֣תָה יִקְצֹ֑רוּ קָמָ֣ה אֵֽין־ ל֗וֹ צֶ֚מַח בְּלִ֣י יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ קֶּ֔מַח אוּלַ֣י יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה זָרִ֖ים יִבְלָעֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Israel is swallowed up! Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.
passages.sermon:
Israel is swallowed up.
Now Israel lives among the nations.
Israel is like a vessel that no one wants.
Israel has become worthless among the nations.
passages.original: נִבְלַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַתָּה֙ הָי֣וּ בַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּכְלִ֖י אֵֽין־ חֵ֥פֶץ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.
passages.sermon:
Israel acted alone.
Israel went up to Assyria.
Israel was like a wild donkey by itself.
Ephraim paid for allies.
Ephraim hired lovers.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הֵ֙מָּה֙ עָל֣וּ אַשּׁ֔וּר פֶּ֖רֶא בּוֹדֵ֣ד ל֑וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם הִתְנ֥וּ אֲהָבִֽים

passages.text: Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.
passages.sermon:
Israel tries to hire allies from other nations.
God says, "I will gather them together now."
They will become fewer in number.
A powerful king will oppress them.
This king will rule over many princes.
Israel will suffer under his rule.
passages.original: גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־ יִתְנ֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֖ם עַתָּ֣ה אֲקַבְּצֵ֑ם וַיָּחֵ֣לּוּ מְּעָ֔ט מִמַּשָּׂ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ שָׂרִֽים׃

passages.text: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, they became his altars for sinning.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim built many altars.
Ephraim made these altars for sinning.
These altars became places where Ephraim sinned.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִרְבָּ֥ה אֶפְרַ֛יִם מִזְבְּחֹ֖ת לַחֲטֹ֑א הָיוּ־ ל֥וֹ מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לַחֲטֹֽא׃

passages.text: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law, they regarded them as something strange.
passages.sermon:
God gave His law to Israel.
God wrote many great things in His law for Israel.
Israel saw God's law as something foreign.
Israel did not accept God's law as their own.
passages.original: אֶכְתּוֹב ל֔וֹ רִבּוֹ תּֽוֹרָתִ֑י כְּמוֹ־ זָ֖ר נֶחְשָֽׁבוּ׃

passages.text: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The people offer sacrifices as gifts to the LORD.
They kill animals and eat the meat.
The LORD does not accept their sacrifices.
The LORD will remember their sins.
The LORD will punish them for their wrongdoings.
They will go back to Egypt.
passages.original: זִבְחֵ֣י הַבְהָבַ֗י יִזְבְּח֤וּ בָשָׂר֙ וַיֹּאכֵ֔לוּ יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א רָצָ֑ם עַתָּ֞ה יִזְכֹּ֤ר עֲוֺנָם֙ וְיִפְקֹ֣ד חַטֹּאותָ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה מִצְרַ֥יִם יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃

passages.text: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has multiplied its fortified cities. But I will send fire upon their cities, and it will consume their citadels.
passages.sermon:
Israel forgot his Maker.
Israel built palaces.
Judah built many fortified cities.
I will send fire on their cities.
The fire will destroy their strongholds.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ עֹשֵׂ֗הוּ וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ הֵֽיכָל֔וֹת וִֽיהוּדָ֕ה הִרְבָּ֖ה עָרִ֣ים בְּצֻר֑וֹת וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־ אֵ֣שׁ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃ס
